findings.message: Fence closure: checkpoint-push must push the checkpoint and re-fire a failed push. The only git wrapper is squatch/git.py, and on main it has init, status, rev_parse, diff, add, commit, branch, worktree, rebase, restore, merge_squash and describe, but no push. No squatch module invokes git push. Building the seed therefore forces a new public push operation in squatch/git.py and its test. The section 20 registry grants checkpoint-push only `checkpoint/daemon, tests/test_checkpoint.py`, and this ticket fixes that as owns [squatch/checkpoint.py, tests/test_checkpoint.py] + hooks [squatch/daemon.py]. The seed as authored would escape its fence or bypass git.py. Section 20 grants the fence explicitly and the continuation must author exactly that machinery, so this is a plan defect, not something the author can fix.

findings.message: Section 20 and this ticket require the drain to suppress 'only work whose stage equals the tripped emitting_stage' at dispatch selection, before `_draw_retry` (line 226), while unrelated work remains eligible. The bootstrap drain selects whole tickets (`_eligible`/`_reoffer`/`sort_key`). Every offer is a full implement->check->review->merge run, and no ticket or re-offer carries a selectable stage. As a result, an `implement` trip (the common `emitting_stage`) matches every offer and acts as a global pause with no 'unrelated work' to keep eligible. A `check`/`review`/`triage` trip matches no offer, so the hold is inert. That leaves the first acceptance criterion either vacuous or in contradiction with the ban on global suppression. The plan never defines how a trip's `emitting_stage` maps onto a drain offer.
